agenda: Discuss the benefits and concerns regarding the installation of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community grid
Evaluate the impact of limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm
Consider how the online posting of air quality readings might affect community awareness and engagement
Discuss any additional measures residents would like to see included in the policy to protect community health and well-being

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss the benefits and concerns regarding the installation of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community grid
transcript.text: As someone who lives near University Hill and rents my home, I appreciate the addition of real-time air quality monitors near schools and throughout our community. Knowing that these monitors will provide data to protect sensitive groups like children and the elderly during construction gives me some peace of mind, especially since construction can impact local air quality significantly [2, 3, 5]. However, I would like to understand how accessible this data will be to residents like myself and how quickly any air quality issues will be addressed.

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss the benefits and concerns regarding the installation of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community grid
transcript.text: As a renter in Lincoln Hill who drives regularly, I see the value in having real-time air quality monitors especially near schools and residential areas to ensure construction doesn't harm our health. Knowing the data will be posted online helps me feel more informed and secure about air quality during this project. It’s important that NYSDOT acts promptly if any air quality issues arise from construction activities to protect our community [1, 4].

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss the benefits and concerns regarding the installation of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community grid
transcript.text: As a young resident living in group quarters in Lincoln Hill, I don't drive or work currently, so my exposure to construction-related traffic might be limited, but I still spend time near schools and community areas. The commitment to install real-time air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community, with data posted online, is reassuring because it shows NYSDOT will actively track air quality impacts during construction. This transparency is important to me because even without commuting, poor air quality can affect my health. I also appreciate that the monitoring program will be overseen by NYSDOT and that protocols will be in place to address any air quality exceedances, which helps protect vulnerable groups in our community [1, 5].

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss the benefits and concerns regarding the installation of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community grid
transcript.text: As a longtime resident of Washington Square and a homeowner, I truly appreciate the commitment to install real-time air quality monitors near schools and throughout our community, especially given my age and the potential sensitivity to air quality issues [1, 3]. Knowing that NYSDOT will oversee this monitoring and have protocols to address any exceedances provides reassurance that our health will be protected during construction. I also welcome the transparency of posting data online so residents like me can stay informed without needing to commute or be directly involved daily [1].

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss the benefits and concerns regarding the installation of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community grid
transcript.text: As a young resident living in group quarters near South Campus, I spend a lot of time around schools and community areas, so the installation of real-time air quality monitors and having the data available online really helps me feel safer. Even though I don't commute or work currently, poor air quality from construction could affect my health, so I appreciate NYSDOT's commitment to monitoring and addressing any issues promptly during the project [1, 2]. This transparency and oversight make me more comfortable with the ongoing construction near my neighborhood.

transcript.agenda_item: Evaluate the impact of limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm
transcript.text: As an 84-year-old homeowner in South Valley, I find the proposal to limit construction near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm very considerate. It would help reduce noise and disturbances during early mornings, evenings, and weekends when we most want peace and quiet, especially since the current policy allows work as early as 6 am and as late as 9 pm [1, 2]. This change could significantly improve our quality of life during construction, so I am inclined to support it.

transcript.agenda_item: Evaluate the impact of limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm
transcript.text: As a renter with a disability living in Near Eastside, limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm would greatly help me avoid excessive noise and disruption during early mornings, evenings, and weekends, which are important times for rest and managing my health. This change seems more considerate of residents' wellbeing and aligns with efforts to minimize neighborhood impacts during construction [1, 3, 5]. I support this limitation as it would improve my quality of life during the project.

transcript.agenda_item: Evaluate the impact of limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm
transcript.text: As a 70-year-old homeowner who lives free and clear in Meadowbrook, I appreciate the proposal to limit construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm. This change would help reduce noise and disruptions during early mornings, evenings, and weekends, which is important for my comfort and peace, especially since I am often at home throughout the day [3]. Knowing that construction vibration and noise are currently allowed between 6 am and 9 pm, this restriction feels like a needed improvement to lessen the impact on residents like me [3]. I support this measure as it balances construction needs with neighborhood quality of life [1, 3].

transcript.agenda_item: Evaluate the impact of limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm
transcript.text: As someone who works from home in Tipp Hill and owns my home with a mortgage, limiting construction hours near residences to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm would help reduce noise disruptions during times I am most likely to be working or resting at home. Currently, construction can occur as early as 6 am and as late as 9 pm, which can be very disruptive to my work-from-home schedule and overall peace [2, 3]. I appreciate that this change balances construction needs with protecting neighborhood quality of life during the project.

transcript.agenda_item: Evaluate the impact of limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm
transcript.text: As a South Valley renter who commutes by car, limiting construction near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm would help reduce noise during times I am likely to be at home resting or preparing for my commute. Given that current construction hours are from 6 am to 9 pm, this change feels like a reasonable balance between allowing construction progress and respecting residents' quality of life, especially since it would lessen disturbances in early mornings and evenings [2, 3]. I support this measure as it acknowledges the impact on our neighborhood while keeping necessary work on schedule.

transcript.agenda_item: Consider how the online posting of air quality readings might affect community awareness and engagement
transcript.text: As someone living in group quarters in North Valley with a disability, having real-time air quality monitors online could really help me stay aware of the air quality near my home and school, which is important for managing my health. I appreciate that this transparency can keep the community informed and possibly prompt quicker action if pollution gets too high during construction, which aligns with the monitoring program described [4, 5]. Knowing when air quality is safe or not could help me plan my day better and protect my wellbeing.

transcript.agenda_item: Consider how the online posting of air quality readings might affect community awareness and engagement
transcript.text: As an 86-year-old homeowner with a disability, I find the commitment to post real-time air quality readings online very reassuring. Being able to check air quality near my home helps me manage my health better, especially during construction when dust and emissions might increase. Also, limiting construction near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm would reduce noise that disrupts my rest and daily routine, which is critical for my well-being [4, 3]. I support these measures as they address both health and peace in our community.

transcript.agenda_item: Consider how the online posting of air quality readings might affect community awareness and engagement
transcript.text: As a 72-year-old homeowner in the University Neighborhood, I appreciate the plan to post real-time air quality readings online. This transparency helps me stay informed about environmental conditions near my home, which is important for my health and peace of mind, especially with construction nearby. Limiting construction hours to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm would also reduce noise disruptions during times I am most likely to be home, enhancing my comfort and quality of life [3, 4]. Overall, I support these commitments as they balance construction progress with protecting residents' wellbeing.

transcript.agenda_item: Consider how the online posting of air quality readings might affect community awareness and engagement
transcript.text: As a homeowner in Washington Square living on a fixed income, I find the commitment to post real-time air quality readings online very important. It will help me stay informed about any changes in air pollution during construction, which could affect my health and the comfort of my home environment. Also, limiting construction hours to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm would reduce noise disturbances during the early mornings and evenings when I am usually at home, which is crucial for my rest and peace [3, 4]. I support these measures because they balance necessary construction work with protecting residents like me.

transcript.agenda_item: Consider how the online posting of air quality readings might affect community awareness and engagement
transcript.text: As a renter with a disability in the University Neighborhood, I am encouraged by the commitment to post real-time air quality readings online because it will help me monitor environmental conditions that could affect my health, especially during construction. Knowing the air quality near my home at any time will allow me to better manage my disability and avoid exposure to harmful pollutants. Also, limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm seems reasonable since it reduces noise disruptions that could impact my rest and well-being [3, 4]. These measures show a thoughtful balance between construction progress and protecting vulnerable community members like myself.

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss any additional measures residents would like to see included in the policy to protect community health and well-being
transcript.text: As a homeowner in Sedgwick with a mortgage and someone who commutes by car, I really appreciate the addition of air quality monitors around schools and the community, as well as the plan to post readings online. This transparency will help me and my neighbors stay informed about any pollution that might affect our health during construction. Also, limiting construction near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm is very important to reduce noise during my early mornings and evenings when I am home resting or preparing for my commute. These measures seem like a reasonable balance between progress and protecting our quality of life.

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss any additional measures residents would like to see included in the policy to protect community health and well-being
transcript.text: As a resident with a disability living in group quarters here in North Valley, I really welcome the addition of air quality monitors near schools and throughout the community, as well as posting the readings online. This transparency is crucial for me to monitor and manage my health during the construction period. Also, I strongly support limiting construction hours near homes to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm, as this will help reduce noise disruptions that can negatively affect my rest and well-being. These measures seem like important steps toward protecting vulnerable community members like myself while construction is underway [2, 3, 4].

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss any additional measures residents would like to see included in the policy to protect community health and well-being
transcript.text: As a renter living in Southside with no income, I appreciate that the policy adds air quality monitors near schools and community areas with real-time data posted online, as this helps protect vulnerable residents like me from harmful pollution during construction. Limiting construction noise to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm near homes would also reduce disturbances during times when people need rest, which is important for my well-being in a busy neighborhood. These measures show consideration for environmental justice concerns that affect low-income and minority residents in our community, like the construction impacts and health risks discussed in the policy [1, 3, 4].

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss any additional measures residents would like to see included in the policy to protect community health and well-being
transcript.text: As a renter in Eastwood who commutes by car, I value the proposed network of air quality monitors near schools and community areas with online postings. This transparency helps me stay informed about pollution levels during construction, which is important since I live near busy roads and want to protect my health. Limiting construction hours to 7 am to 7 pm on weekdays also makes sense to reduce noise disruptions during my evening and early morning rest times. These measures seem like a reasonable way to balance project progress with community well-being [3, 4].

transcript.agenda_item: Discuss any additional measures residents would like to see included in the policy to protect community health and well-being
transcript.text: As a renter with a disability living in Lincoln Hill and no income, I strongly support adding the network of air quality monitors near schools and community areas with readings posted online. This transparency is vital for me to track air quality and protect my health during construction, since emissions from equipment and traffic can affect vulnerable people like me [3, 4]. Limiting construction near homes to 7 am to 7 pm on weekdays would also help reduce noise disturbances that interfere with my rest and well-being [2]. These measures would show real consideration for people in my situation.

meetings.summary: Residents from University Hill, Lincoln Hill, Washington Square, South Campus, South Valley, Near Eastside, Meadowbrook, Tipp Hill, North Valley, Franklin Square, University Neighborhood, Sedgwick, Southside, and Eastwood have expressed strong support for installing real-time air quality monitors near schools and community areas, emphasizing their importance for protecting vulnerable groups, including low-income renters and those with disabilities, during construction. Many residents, including those from Southside, Sedgwick, Eastwood, and now Lincoln Hill, appreciate the transparency of posting real-time air quality data online and endorse limiting construction hours to weekdays from 7 am to 7 pm to reduce noise and disturbances, highlighting benefits for health, rest, and quality of life. Vulnerable community members, such as a North Valley resident with a disability, a Southside renter with no income, and a Lincoln Hill renter with a disability and no income, specifically noted these measures as crucial for managing health risks and environmental justice concerns related to construction impacts. An Eastwood renter who commutes by car emphasized the importance of these measures for staying informed about pollution near busy roads and balancing project progress with community well-being. Overall, the community consistently values transparency, health protection, noise reduction, and consideration for environmental justice in construction policies.
